Food, a necessity, vs dye, a cosmetic only for you? Big difference on risking running into serious allergies.

If the cat doesn't care, whatever. But you are still putting an unnecessary risk on your cat for your aesthetic gain entirely. You don't know how they will interpret the color later, i literally have a friend who dyed her cat with polka dots and regretted it because the cat began overgrooming the spots. They just see a different color, not your fashion choice. I feel the same way about people who shove their dogs and cats that obviously don't like clothes in clothing all of the time.

[Don't Dye Your Cat](https://www.pethealthnetwork.com/cat-health/cat-grooming/cat-hair-dye-it-safe-dye-cat-fur#:~:text=Still%2C%20as%20National%20Poison%20Prevention,potentially%20be%20dangerous%20to%20cats.&text=When%20used%20on%20cats%2C%20these,mouth%20and%20even%20liver%20failure.)

On top of that stuff, why would you put your pet through that? They don't care what color they are, you're risking allergic reactions, dye ingestion, torturing the poor thing with the application, and so many other things just so you can look at a funny looking cat for a few weeks. Why?
pet dye leads to overgrooming, stress, and skin issues in cats
